# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:24:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# gh-1590: [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%); repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

## Summary
Session JSONL files grow without a practical bound. On one machine 175 sessions occupy 8.6 GB; the largest is 1.1 GB, of which the actual conversation is ~0.5%. The append-only `custom` ledgers dominate, `fa session repair --dry-run` cannot show the reduction it would give, and resuming a huge file is slow. Related: #1572-#1575.

## Evidence (fa 1.0.565, macOS)
`~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/--Users-…-postal-nl--/2026-09-18T19-33-24-152105_01a0b55d-….jsonl` — 1,176,312,924 bytes. Per-line breakdown (python scan):

| record | count | size | max line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom:model_request_summary` | 1216 | **1034 MB (88%)** | 2.7 MB |
| `custom:shell_job_registry` | 1635 | **136 MB (12%)** | 123 KB |
| `message` | 2441 | 5.1 MB (0.4%) | 325 KB |
| `trajectory_manifest_blob` / `prompt_blob` | 12 + 12 | 0.8 MB | 47 KB |

Per-day `model_request_summary`: 2026-09-23 — 699 records, 920 MB; those records carry up to 1693 full-text message summaries (`preview` + `blocks[].text`) each. A single record on 09-28 holds 2222 messages (2.7 MB). Another large session (this repo, 757 MB) is still adding `model_request_summary` at ~8.9 MB/day and `shell_job_registry` at ~4.5 MB/day even on current builds.

## Problems
1. **`model_request_summary` stores a full per-message snapshot of every outbound request.** `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_record.dart`, applied in `agent_loop.dart` `_buildModelRequestEvent`, landed 2026-10-05) keeps the newest 64 messages / 256 KiB of text full, but sessions written before it (or by older binaries) still hold the unbounded form, and nothing migrates them. Even the capped form re-embeds up to 256 KiB of already-persisted message text per request (≈ O(requests × 256 KiB)); the records can reference messages by id/hash instead.
2. **`shell_job_registry` still appends one full snapshot per change** (1635 records, up to 123 KB each in this file; ~205 records/4.5 MB in one current day of a live session). The in-memory deduper only suppresses byte-identical snapshots; there is no rotation/compaction at write time, and only the latest snapshot is ever read.
3. **`fa session repair` dry-run shows no reduction.** `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returns `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`, the dry-run branch), so the summary line reads `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` and `855.7 MB → 855.7 MB` although the dry-run counts do list the drops. The command help claims it shrinks the file. The real repair works: I copied the 1.1 GB file and ran `fa session repair` → **1.10 GiB → 4.9 MB** in ~5 s (dropped model_request_summary×1216, shell_job_registry×1634, kept latest 1; original kept as `.bak`). So the misleading output (and users not applying it) is the bug, not the rewrite itself. A dry-run should report the projected `bytesAfter` (sum of kept spans), and the dropped-bytes per type.
4. **Resume of big sessions is slow.** `boot_stage context` ≈ 4.6 s for an 880 MB file — the loader still has to scan the ledger bytes it never uses.

## Expected
- `model_request_summary` persists hashes/metadata (message ids/hashes + sizes, tool names, prompt/manifest hashes) — not message text; text is looked up from the `message` records.
- `shell_job_registry` bounded at write time (rotate/overwrite: keep only the latest snapshot, or compact on session close/rotation).
- `fa session repair --dry-run` prints the projected size (`bytesAfter` = kept span bytes) and reclaimed bytes per ledger type.
- Optional: automatic ledger compaction when a session file crosses a threshold (e.g. on resume), so users need not know about `repair`; resume of an 880 MB file should not pay 4.6 s of scanning.

## Acceptance
- Test: dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture.
- Test: a 1000-message request produces a `model_request_summary` of bounded size independent of message text length.
- Test: N shell-job state changes leave ≤ 1 (or a small constant of) `shell_job_registry` records in the file.
- A multi-hundred-MB fixture resumes with `boot_stage context` below an agreed budget.

Now let me think about the throttle semantics carefully.

`LedgerSnapshotThrottle`:
- `shouldPersistNow()`: if never persisted or window passed → `true`. Otherwise, reserve pending (`_pendingSince ??= now`), arm timer, return false.
- `poll()`: if pending and `now - since >= minInterval` → consume pending, return true.
- `confirmPersisted()`: `_lastPersistAt = now`, clear pending, cancel timer.
- `reset()`: clear everything, cancel timer.
- `dispose()`: cancel timer only.
- `_arm()`: `Timer(minInterval, ...)` — after minInterval, poll; if due, call onFlushDue.

Potential issue #1: **The trailing timer arms for `minInterval` from the time of refusal, but `poll()` requires `_clock().difference(since) >= minInterval` where `since` is when the FIRST refused mutation happened.** The timer fires at `refusalTime + minInterval`. `since` ≤ refusalTime (the first refusal could be earlier than the current refusal). So when the timer fires, `now - since >= minInterval` holds since `since <= refusalTime` and `now = refusalTime + minInterval`. OK that's fine. But what if `since` is much earlier — e.g., the first refusal happened, timer armed; timer fires at `first_refusal + minInterval` (well, at `armTime + minInterval`). Actually the timer arms only once (`if (_timer != null) return`). So the timer fires at `armTime + minInterval`, and since `since <= armTime`, `poll()` returns true. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle race: what if the timer callback runs and `poll()` returns false because... `poll` returns false when `_pendingSince == null` (already flushed via confirmPersisted... no, confirmPersisted clears pending AND cancels timer). Hmm, `confirmPersisted` cancels the timer, so the callback wouldn't run. `reset` cancels too. `dispose` cancels. So `poll() == false` inside the timer callback only if... `poll()` already consumed pending — but only the timer callback calls poll in production. So mostly fine. Actually, if `_arm()` is called but the timer already fired and callback in progress... not a real concern.

Potential issue #2: **Timer arm vs. `pendingSince` mismatch when `confirmPersisted` is called via the flush callback.** In `_persistJobBoard`, when the trailing flush runs (unforced re-entry via `onFlushDue` → `_persistJobBoard()`), the flow:
1. `records.isEmpty` → return (no confirm) — pending already consumed by poll, timer disarmed itself (`_timer = null` in callback). Fine.
2. `shouldPersistNow()` — if the window since `_lastPersistAt` has passed (30 since last persist), returns `true` → persist. OK.
   But if window since last persist has NOT passed (e.g., the first mutation persisted at t=0, refused mutations reserved pending at t=10, timer armed at t=10 fires at t=40 → poll: `40 - 10 >= 30` → true, consumed. Then `_persistJobBoard` → `shouldPersistNow()`: `now(40) - lastPersist(0) = 40 >= 30` → true → persist. Good.
   
   But consider: mutations at t=0 (persist, last=0), refused at t=29 (pendingSince=29, timer armed fires t=59). At t=45, run finalize calls `_persistJobBoard()` unforced: `45 - 0 = 45 >= 30` → true → persists. `confirmPersisted` sets last=45, pending=null, cancels timer. Good.
   
   Now what about: persist at t=0 (last=0). Mutation refused at t=10 (pending=10, timer armed → fires at 40). At t=35, another mutation: `35 - 0 = 35 >= 30` → shouldPersistNow returns TRUE immediately. So persist happens, confirmPersisted: last=35, pending=null (clears the reservation!), cancels timer. Fine — the state landed anyway.

3. Deduper suppresses identical payload → return without confirming throttle. Hmm! Here's a subtle issue: In the flush path, `shouldPersistNow()` returned true, but then `deduper.shouldPersist(json)` returns false (byte-identical to last persisted) → `return` — the throttle is NOT confirmed. So `_lastPersistAt` stays at the older time and `_pendingSince` was already consumed by `poll()`. Window still measured from last real append. That's fine — nothing changed, so nothing needed persisting. Actually wait: shouldPersistNow() returned true (allowed), and then nothing persisted. The window continues from the previous append. That's semantically fine (deduper suppresses no-ops). But there's an edge: `shouldPersistNow()` returned true without any "reservation" semantics; fine.

   However, there's an asymmetry: when `shouldPersistNow()` returns true but the deduper refuses, the throttle's `_pendingSince` (if it was reserved by an earlier refusal and NOT yet consumed by poll) stays reserved with the timer armed. The timer will fire later and re-run `_persistJobBoard()`, which will encode + dedupe-refuse again → no-op. Minor wasted encode. Not a bug.

Potential issue #3: **force path doesn't confirm throttle timing bookkeeping properly.** `_flushJobBoardPersist()` → `dispose()` then `_persistJobBoard(force: true)`. In the forced persist: records non-empty; `force` skips the gate; deduper check; append; `confirmPersisted()` on throttle sets `_lastPersistAt = now`, clears pending, cancels timer (already disposed). Good.

   But if the forced persist finds records EMPTY (board with no cards), it returns early — and `_pendingSince` might still be set, but the timer was disposed so no flush will fire. Fine at shutdown.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:24:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).

# gh-1590: [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%); repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

## Summary
Session JSONL files grow without a practical bound. On one machine 175 sessions occupy 8.6 GB; the largest is 1.1 GB, of which the actual conversation is ~0.5%. The append-only `custom` ledgers dominate, `fa session repair --dry-run` cannot show the reduction it would give, and resuming a huge file is slow. Related: #1572-#1575.

## Evidence (fa 1.0.565, macOS)
`~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/--Users-…-postal-nl--/2026-09-18T19-33-24-152105_01a0b55d-….jsonl` — 1,176,312,924 bytes. Per-line breakdown (python scan):

| record | count | size | max line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom:model_request_summary` | 1216 | **1034 MB (88%)** | 2.7 MB |
| `custom:shell_job_registry` | 1635 | **136 MB (12%)** | 123 KB |
| `message` | 2441 | 5.1 MB (0.4%) | 325 KB |
| `trajectory_manifest_blob` / `prompt_blob` | 12 + 12 | 0.8 MB | 47 KB |

Per-day `model_request_summary`: 2026-09-23 — 699 records, 920 MB; those records carry up to 1693 full-text message summaries (`preview` + `blocks[].text`) each. A single record on 09-28 holds 2222 messages (2.7 MB). Another large session (this repo, 757 MB) is still adding `model_request_summary` at ~8.9 MB/day and `shell_job_registry` at ~4.5 MB/day even on current builds.

## Problems
1. **`model_request_summary` stores a full per-message snapshot of every outbound request.** `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_record.dart`, applied in `agent_loop.dart` `_buildModelRequestEvent`, landed 2026-10-05) keeps the newest 64 messages / 256 KiB of text full, but sessions written before it (or by older binaries) still hold the unbounded form, and nothing migrates them. Even the capped form re-embeds up to 256 KiB of already-persisted message text per request (≈ O(requests × 256 KiB)); the records can reference messages by id/hash instead.
2. **`shell_job_registry` still appends one full snapshot per change** (1635 records, up to 123 KB each in this file; ~205 records/4.5 MB in one current day of a live session). The in-memory deduper only suppresses byte-identical snapshots; there is no rotation/compaction at write time, and only the latest snapshot is ever read.
3. **`fa session repair` dry-run shows no reduction.** `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returns `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`, the dry-run branch), so the summary line reads `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` and `855.7 MB → 855.7 MB` although the dry-run counts do list the drops. The command help claims it shrinks the file. The real repair works: I copied the 1.1 GB file and ran `fa session repair` → **1.10 GiB → 4.9 MB** in ~5 s (dropped model_request_summary×1216, shell_job_registry×1634, kept latest 1; original kept as `.bak`). So the misleading output (and users not applying it) is the bug, not the rewrite itself. A dry-run should report the projected `bytesAfter` (sum of kept spans), and the dropped-bytes per type.
4. **Resume of big sessions is slow.** `boot_stage context` ≈ 4.6 s for an 880 MB file — the loader still has to scan the ledger bytes it never uses.

## Expected
- `model_request_summary` persists hashes/metadata (message ids/hashes + sizes, tool names, prompt/manifest hashes) — not message text; text is looked up from the `message` records.
- `shell_job_registry` bounded at write time (rotate/overwrite: keep only the latest snapshot, or compact on session close/rotation).
- `fa session repair --dry-run` prints the projected size (`bytesAfter` = kept span bytes) and reclaimed bytes per ledger type.
- Optional: automatic ledger compaction when a session file crosses a threshold (e.g. on resume), so users need not know about `repair`; resume of an 880 MB file should not pay 4.6 s of scanning.

## Acceptance
- Test: dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture.
- Test: a 1000-message request produces a `model_request_summary` of bounded size independent of message text length.
- Test: N shell-job state changes leave ≤ 1 (or a small constant of) `shell_job_registry` records in the file.
- A multi-hundred-MB fixture resumes with `boot_stage context` below an agreed budget.

Now let me think about the throttle semantics carefully.

`LedgerSnapshotThrottle`:
- `shouldPersistNow()`: if never persisted or window passed → `true`. Otherwise, reserve pending (`_pendingSince ??= now`), arm timer, return false.
- `poll()`: if pending and `now - since >= minInterval` → consume pending, return true.
- `confirmPersisted()`: `_lastPersistAt = now`, clear pending, cancel timer.
- `reset()`: clear everything, cancel timer.
- `dispose()`: cancel timer only.
- `_arm()`: `Timer(minInterval, ...)` — after minInterval, poll; if due, call onFlushDue.

Potential issue #1: **The trailing timer arms for `minInterval` from the time of refusal, but `poll()` requires `_clock().difference(since) >= minInterval` where `since` is when the FIRST refused mutation happened.** The timer fires at `refusalTime + minInterval`. `since` ≤ refusalTime (the first refusal could be earlier than the current refusal). So when the timer fires, `now - since >= minInterval` holds since `since <= refusalTime` and `now = refusalTime + minInterval`. OK that's fine. But what if `since` is much earlier — e.g., the first refusal happened, timer armed; timer fires at `first_refusal + minInterval` (well, at `armTime + minInterval`). Actually the timer arms only once (`if (_timer != null) return`). So the timer fires at `armTime + minInterval`, and since `since <= armTime`, `poll()` returns true. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle race: what if the timer callback runs and `poll()` returns false because... `poll` returns false when `_pendingSince == null` (already flushed via confirmPersisted... no, confirmPersisted clears pending AND cancels timer). Hmm, `confirmPersisted` cancels the timer, so the callback wouldn't run. `reset` cancels too. `dispose` cancels. So `poll() == false` inside the timer callback only if... `poll()` already consumed pending — but only the timer callback calls poll in production. So mostly fine. Actually, if `_arm()` is called but the timer already fired and callback in progress... not a real concern.

Potential issue #2: **Timer arm vs. `pendingSince` mismatch when `confirmPersisted` is called via the flush callback.** In `_persistJobBoard`, when the trailing flush runs (unforced re-entry via `onFlushDue` → `_persistJobBoard()`), the flow:
1. `records.isEmpty` → return (no confirm) — pending already consumed by poll, timer disarmed itself (`_timer = null` in callback). Fine.
2. `shouldPersistNow()` — if the window since `_lastPersistAt` has passed (30 since last persist), returns `true` → persist. OK.
   But if window since last persist has NOT passed (e.g., the first mutation persisted at t=0, refused mutations reserved pending at t=10, timer armed at t=10 fires at t=40 → poll: `40 - 10 >= 30` → true, consumed. Then `_persistJobBoard` → `shouldPersistNow()`: `now(40) - lastPersist(0) = 40 >= 30` → true → persist. Good.

   Now what about: persist at t=0 (last=0). Mutation refused at t=10 (pending=10, timer armed → fires at 40). At t=35, another mutation: `35 - 0 = 35 >= 30` → shouldPersistNow returns TRUE immediately. So persist happens, confirmPersisted: last=35, pending=null (clears the reservation!), cancels timer. Fine — the state landed anyway.

3. Deduper suppresses identical payload → return without confirming throttle. Hmm! Here's a subtle issue: In the flush path, `shouldPersistNow()` returned true, but then `deduper.shouldPersist(json)` returns false (byte-identical to last persisted) → `return` — the throttle is NOT confirmed. So `_lastPersistAt` stays at the older time and `_pendingSince` was already consumed by `poll()`. Window still measured from last real append. That's fine — nothing changed, so nothing needed persisting. Actually wait: shouldPersistNow() returned true (allowed), and then nothing persisted. The window continues from the previous append. That's semantically fine (deduper suppresses no-ops). But there's an edge: `shouldPersistNow()` returned true without any "reservation" semantics; fine.

   However, there's an asymmetry: when `shouldPersistNow()` returns true but the deduper refuses, the throttle's `_pendingSince` (if it was reserved by an earlier refusal and NOT yet consumed by poll) stays reserved with the timer armed. The timer will fire later and re-run `_persistJobBoard()`, which will encode + dedupe-refuse again → no-op. Minor wasted encode. Not a bug.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:24:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# gh-1590: [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%); repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

## Summary
Session JSONL files grow without a practical bound. On one machine 175 sessions occupy 8.6 GB; the largest is 1.1 GB, of which the actual conversation is ~0.5%. The append-only `custom` ledgers dominate, `fa session repair --dry-run` cannot show the reduction it would give, and resuming a huge file is slow. Related: #1572-#1575.

## Evidence (fa 1.0.565, macOS)
`~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/--Users-…-postal-nl--/2026-09-18T19-33-24-152105_01a0b55d-….jsonl` — 1,176,312,924 bytes. Per-line breakdown (python scan):

| record | count | size | max line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom:model_request_summary` | 1216 | **1034 MB (88%)** | 2.7 MB |
| `custom:shell_job_registry` | 1635 | **136 MB (12%)** | 123 KB |
| `message` | 2441 | 5.1 MB (0.4%) | 325 KB |
| `trajectory_manifest_blob` / `prompt_blob` | 12 + 12 | 0.8 MB | 47 KB |

Per-day `model_request_summary`: 2026-09-23 — 699 records, 920 MB; those records carry up to 1693 full-text message summaries (`preview` + `blocks[].text`) each. A single record on 09-28 holds 2222 messages (2.7 MB). Another large session (this repo, 757 MB) is still adding `model_request_summary` at ~8.9 MB/day and `shell_job_registry` at ~4.5 MB/day even on current builds.

## Problems
1. **`model_request_summary` stores a full per-message snapshot of every outbound request.** `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_record.dart`, applied in `agent_loop.dart` `_buildModelRequestEvent`, landed 2026-10-05) keeps the newest 64 messages / 256 KiB of text full, but sessions written before it (or by older binaries) still hold the unbounded form, and nothing migrates them. Even the capped form re-embeds up to 256 KiB of already-persisted message text per request (≈ O(requests × 256 KiB)); the records can reference messages by id/hash instead.
2. **`shell_job_registry` still appends one full snapshot per change** (1635 records, up to 123 KB each in this file; ~205 records/4.5 MB in one current day of a live session). The in-memory deduper only suppresses byte-identical snapshots; there is no rotation/compaction at write time, and only the latest snapshot is ever read.
3. **`fa session repair` dry-run shows no reduction.** `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returns `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`, the dry-run branch), so the summary line reads `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` and `855.7 MB → 855.7 MB` although the dry-run counts do list the drops. The command help claims it shrinks the file. The real repair works: I copied the 1.1 GB file and ran `fa session repair` → **1.10 GiB → 4.9 MB** in ~5 s (dropped model_request_summary×1216, shell_job_registry×1634, kept latest 1; original kept as `.bak`). So the misleading output (and users not applying it) is the bug, not the rewrite itself. A dry-run should report the projected `bytesAfter` (sum of kept spans), and the dropped-bytes per type.
4. **Resume of big sessions is slow.** `boot_stage context` ≈ 4.6 s for an 880 MB file — the loader still has to scan the ledger bytes it never uses.

## Expected
- `model_request_summary` persists hashes/metadata (message ids/hashes + sizes, tool names, prompt/manifest hashes) — not message text; text is looked up from the `message` records.
- `shell_job_registry` bounded at write time (rotate/overwrite: keep only the latest snapshot, or compact on session close/rotation).
- `fa session repair --dry-run` prints the projected size (`bytesAfter` = kept span bytes) and reclaimed bytes per ledger type.
- Optional: automatic ledger compaction when a session file crosses a threshold (e.g. on resume), so users need not know about `repair`; resume of an 880 MB file should not pay 4.6 s of scanning.

## Acceptance
- Test: dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture.
- Test: a 1000-message request produces a `model_request_summary` of bounded size independent of message text length.
- Test: N shell-job state changes leave ≤ 1 (or a small constant of) `shell_job_registry` records in the file.
- A multi-hundred-MB fixture resumes with `boot_stage context` below an agreed budget.

Now let me think about the throttle semantics carefully.

`LedgerSnapshotThrottle`:
- `shouldPersistNow()`: if never persisted or window passed → `true`. Otherwise, reserve pending (`_pendingSince ??= now`), arm timer, return false.
- `poll()`: if pending and `now - since >= minInterval` → consume pending, return true.
- `confirmPersisted()`: `_lastPersistAt = now`, clear pending, cancel timer.
- `reset()`: clear everything, cancel timer.
- `dispose()`: cancel timer only.
- `_arm()`: `Timer(minInterval, ...)` — after minInterval, poll; if due, call onFlushDue.

Potential issue #1: **The trailing timer arms for `minInterval` from the time of refusal, but `poll()` requires `_clock().difference(since) >= minInterval` where `since` is when the FIRST refused mutation happened.** The timer fires at `refusalTime + minInterval`. `since` ≤ refusalTime (the first refusal could be earlier than the current refusal). So when the timer fires, `now - since >= minInterval` holds since `since <= refusalTime` and `now = refusalTime + minInterval`. OK that's fine. But what if `since` is much earlier — e.g., the first refusal happened, timer armed; timer fires at `first_refusal + minInterval` (well, at `armTime + minInterval`). Actually the timer arms only once (`if (_timer != null) return`). So the timer fires at `armTime + minInterval`, and since `since <= armTime`, `poll()` returns true. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle race: what if the timer callback runs and `poll()` returns false because... `poll` returns false when `_pendingSince == null` (already flushed via confirmPersisted... no, confirmPersisted clears pending AND cancels timer). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1594
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1594
- **Title**: gh-1590 [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%) repair --dry-run reports no reduction
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1590` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +804
- **Deletions**: -56
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T19:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T21:24:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1590
### Root Cause

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.

# gh-1590: [BUG] session JSONL grows without bound from append-only custom ledgers (model_request_summary 88%, shell_job_registry 12%); repair --dry-run reports no reduction

## Description

## Summary
Session JSONL files grow without a practical bound. On one machine 175 sessions occupy 8.6 GB; the largest is 1.1 GB, of which the actual conversation is ~0.5%. The append-only `custom` ledgers dominate, `fa session repair --dry-run` cannot show the reduction it would give, and resuming a huge file is slow. Related: #1572-#1575.

## Evidence (fa 1.0.565, macOS)
`~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/--Users-…-postal-nl--/2026-09-18T19-33-24-152105_01a0b55d-….jsonl` — 1,176,312,924 bytes. Per-line breakdown (python scan):

| record | count | size | max line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom:model_request_summary` | 1216 | **1034 MB (88%)** | 2.7 MB |
| `custom:shell_job_registry` | 1635 | **136 MB (12%)** | 123 KB |
| `message` | 2441 | 5.1 MB (0.4%) | 325 KB |
| `trajectory_manifest_blob` / `prompt_blob` | 12 + 12 | 0.8 MB | 47 KB |

Per-day `model_request_summary`: 2026-09-23 — 699 records, 920 MB; those records carry up to 1693 full-text message summaries (`preview` + `blocks[].text`) each. A single record on 09-28 holds 2222 messages (2.7 MB). Another large session (this repo, 757 MB) is still adding `model_request_summary` at ~8.9 MB/day and `shell_job_registry` at ~4.5 MB/day even on current builds.

## Problems
1. **`model_request_summary` stores a full per-message snapshot of every outbound request.** `capTrajectoryRequestDetail` (gh-1073, `lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_record.dart`, applied in `agent_loop.dart` `_buildModelRequestEvent`, landed 2026-10-05) keeps the newest 64 messages / 256 KiB of text full, but sessions written before it (or by older binaries) still hold the unbounded form, and nothing migrates them. Even the capped form re-embeds up to 256 KiB of already-persisted message text per request (≈ O(requests × 256 KiB)); the records can reference messages by id/hash instead.
2. **`shell_job_registry` still appends one full snapshot per change** (1635 records, up to 123 KB each in this file; ~205 records/4.5 MB in one current day of a live session). The in-memory deduper only suppresses byte-identical snapshots; there is no rotation/compaction at write time, and only the latest snapshot is ever read.
3. **`fa session repair` dry-run shows no reduction.** `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returns `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`, the dry-run branch), so the summary line reads `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` and `855.7 MB → 855.7 MB` although the dry-run counts do list the drops. The command help claims it shrinks the file. The real repair works: I copied the 1.1 GB file and ran `fa session repair` → **1.10 GiB → 4.9 MB** in ~5 s (dropped model_request_summary×1216, shell_job_registry×1634, kept latest 1; original kept as `.bak`). So the misleading output (and users not applying it) is the bug, not the rewrite itself. A dry-run should report the projected `bytesAfter` (sum of kept spans), and the dropped-bytes per type.
4. **Resume of big sessions is slow.** `boot_stage context` ≈ 4.6 s for an 880 MB file — the loader still has to scan the ledger bytes it never uses.

## Expected
- `model_request_summary` persists hashes/metadata (message ids/hashes + sizes, tool names, prompt/manifest hashes) — not message text; text is looked up from the `message` records.
- `shell_job_registry` bounded at write time (rotate/overwrite: keep only the latest snapshot, or compact on session close/rotation).
- `fa session repair --dry-run` prints the projected size (`bytesAfter` = kept span bytes) and reclaimed bytes per ledger type.
- Optional: automatic ledger compaction when a session file crosses a threshold (e.g. on resume), so users need not know about `repair`; resume of an 880 MB file should not pay 4.6 s of scanning.

## Acceptance
- Test: dry-run `bytesAfter` equals the real-run `bytesAfter` on the same fixture.
- Test: a 1000-message request produces a `model_request_summary` of bounded size independent of message text length.
- Test: N shell-job state changes leave ≤ 1 (or a small constant of) `shell_job_registry` records in the file.
- A multi-hundred-MB fixture resumes with `boot_stage context` below an agreed budget.

Now let me think about the throttle semantics carefully.

`LedgerSnapshotThrottle`:
- `shouldPersistNow()`: if never persisted or window passed → `true`. Otherwise, reserve pending (`_pendingSince ??= now`), arm timer, return false.
- `poll()`: if pending and `now - since >= minInterval` → consume pending, return true.
- `confirmPersisted()`: `_lastPersistAt = now`, clear pending, cancel timer.
- `reset()`: clear everything, cancel timer.
- `dispose()`: cancel timer only.
- `_arm()`: `Timer(minInterval, ...)` — after minInterval, poll; if due, call onFlushDue.

Potential issue #1: **The trailing timer arms for `minInterval` from the time of refusal, but `poll()` requires `_clock().difference(since) >= minInterval` where `since` is when the FIRST refused mutation happened.** The timer fires at `refusalTime + minInterval`. `since` ≤ refusalTime (the first refusal could be earlier than the current refusal). So when the timer fires, `now - since >= minInterval` holds since `since <= refusalTime` and `now = refusalTime + minInterval`. OK that's fine. But what if `since` is much earlier — e.g., the first refusal happened, timer armed; timer fires at `first_refusal + minInterval` (well, at `armTime + minInterval`). Actually the timer arms only once (`if (_timer != null) return`). So the timer fires at `armTime + minInterval`, and since `since <= armTime`, `poll()` returns true. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle race: what if the timer callback runs and `poll()` returns false because... `poll` returns false when `_pendingSince == null` (already flushed via confirmPersisted... no, confirmPersisted clears pending AND cancels timer). Hmm, `confirmPersisted` cancels the timer, so the callback wouldn't run. `reset` cancels too. `dispose` cancels. So `poll() == false` inside the timer callback only if... `poll()` already consumed pending — but only the timer callback calls poll in production. So mostly fine. Actually, if `_arm()` is called but the timer already fired and callback in progress... not a real concern.

Potential issue #2: **Timer arm vs. `pendingSince` mismatch when `confirmPersisted` is called via the flush callback.** In `_persistJobBoard`, when the trailing flush runs (unforced re-entry via `onFlushDue` → `_persistJobBoard()`), the flow:
1. `records.isEmpty` → return (no confirm) — pending already consumed by poll, timer disarmed itself (`_timer = null` in callback). Fine.
2. `shouldPersistNow()` — if the window since `_lastPersistAt` has passed (30 since last persist), returns `true` → persist. OK.
   But if window since last persist has NOT passed (e.g., the first mutation persisted at t=0, refused mutations reserved pending at t=10, timer armed at t=10 fires at t=40 → poll: `40 - 10 >= 30` → true, consumed. Then `_persistJobBoard` → `shouldPersistNow()`: `now(40) - lastPersist(0) = 40 >= 30` → true → persist. Good.
   
   But consider: mutations at t=0 (persist, last=0), refused at t=29 (pendingSince=29, timer armed fires t=59). At t=45, run finalize calls `_persistJobBoard()` unforced: `45 - 0 = 45 >= 30` → true → persists. `confirmPersisted` sets last=45, pending=null, cancels timer. Good.
   
   Now what about: persist at t=0 (last=0). Mutation refused at t=10 (pending=10, timer armed → fires at 40). At t=35, another mutation: `35 - 0 = 35 >= 30` → shouldPersistNow returns TRUE immediately. So persist happens, confirmPersisted: last=35, pending=null (clears the reservation!), cancels timer. Fine — the state landed anyway.

3. Deduper suppresses identical payload → return without confirming throttle. Hmm! Here's a subtle issue: In the flush path, `shouldPersistNow()` returned true, but then `deduper.shouldPersist(json)` returns false (byte-identical to last persisted) → `return` — the throttle is NOT confirmed. So `_lastPersistAt` stays at the older time and `_pendingSince` was already consumed by `poll()`. Window still measured from last real append. That's fine — nothing changed, so nothing needed persisting. Actually wait: shouldPersistNow() returned true (allowed), and then nothing persisted. The window continues from the previous append. That's semantically fine (deduper suppresses no-ops). But there's an edge: `shouldPersistNow()` returned true without any "reservation" semantics; fine.

   However, there's an asymmetry: when `shouldPersistNow()` returns true but the deduper refuses, the throttle's `_pendingSince` (if it was reserved by an earlier refusal and NOT yet consumed by poll) stays reserved with the timer armed. The timer will fire later and re-run `_persistJobBoard()`, which will encode + dedupe-refuse again → no-op. Minor wasted encode. Not a bug.

Good.

   What if the forced persist fails (append error)? `revertFailedPersist` on deduper; rethrow; catchError swallows. The throttle still has `_lastPersistAt` from earlier and pending cleared? # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user

`fa session repair --dry-run` could not show the reduction a real repair gives: `repairSessionLedgers(dryRun: true)` returned `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` (`lib/src/session_repair.dart`), so the CLI printed `1.10 GiB → 1.10 GiB` while the dry-run counts listed the drops — users read it as "nothing to reclaim" and never applied the (working) repair. Growth fed by two write-side defects: `shell_job_registry` appended one full snapshot per board mutation (the deduper only suppressed byte-identical payloads — 1,635 records / 136 MB on the ticket's session, only the latest ever read), and no test pinned the bounded `model_request_summary` size for text-heavy requests.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session_repair.dart`: the dry run projects the rewrite — `bytesAfter` = byte sum of the kept spans (exactly what pass 2 streams), plus dropped-bytes-per-ledger accounting (`reclaimed …: model_request_summary×…`) and a `(projected)` size line.
- `lib/src/session/ledger_caps.dart`: new clock-seamed `LedgerSnapshotThrottle` (30 s window; production Timer leg + `poll()` test seam, same shape as the liveness trackers).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_hub_cli.dart` (+ `agent_cli.dart` field): `_persistJobBoard` persists at most one snapshot per window, the rest coalesce behind a trailing flush; empty boards never append; throttle resets on session rehydrate; `runHeadless` finally and REPL teardown force-flush and disarm; run finalize persists unforced so per-settle reaction runs can't defeat the coalescing.

### Test Coverage

- `test/session/session_repair_test.dart::dry-run projects the bytesAfter…` — dry-run `bytesAfter` == real-run `bytesAfter`, `bytesBefore − bytesAfter == Σ dropped bytes` — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_throttle_wiring_test.dart` — 8 shell-job state changes (4 jobs × start+settle) leave **2** `shell_job_registry` records (was 8), the last with every job `done`; a no-job session appends zero registry records — failed before, PASSED after.
- `test/cli/shell_job_ledger_caps_test.dart` — throttle policy (coalescing, trailing flush, reopen, reset, dispose) — PASSED.
- `test/trajectory/request_detail_cap_test.dart` — 1000-message request with 64 KB texts stays under the char budget and within a small constant of a 1-char-text request — PASSED.
- Full `dart test` run green (unit gate); CI shards re-verify.

### Notes

- Dry-run/real parity is exact for well-formed UTF-8 (spans copy byte-for-byte); torn lines are kept and never parsed.
- Optional ticket items not touched (follow-ups): hash-based `model_request_summary` references, auto-compaction on a size threshold, resume `boot_stage context` budget.
